VPN's - They're great, as long as you can trust them.

Pros:

  • Anonymizes your activity assuming you take the necessary precautions not to dox yourself.

  • Allows you to defeat region codes accessing international content.

  • Relatively cheap.

Cons:

  • Most require a credit card and therefore your identity. You can use bitcoin, but that comes with it's own privacy issues.

  • aggregates all your free speech through a single ISP. If they keep logs and there's a breach, you're fucked.

  • Search warrants will also dox you and your activities.

If you're using the same computer that you do all your identifying activities (banking, bills, shopping, etc) on and then connect to you VPN it's like driving your car with your personalized license plate that everyone knows you by on a different route you've never taken to the grocery store and expecting people not to recognize you. Every little program you have installed identifies you when it phones home. When it does that while you're connected to the VPN, you're no longer anonymous. Dedicate a computer to your VPN activities....or use a dedicated VM for it. And make damn sure that when your VPN is disconnected that ZERO packets are sent over your ISP's network. There are ways to ensure that.

Don't talk about where you live. Don't visit regional, state, city groups, subs, forms. Don't use the same sayings, facts, wording that you use on your non-VPN connect that you do on your VPN connection and visa versa.

Alternatives to a VPN for anonymizing activities:

  • Tor

  • I2P

Tor is a method of anonymizing your internet activities.

I2P is it's own private, encrypted, anonymized network. There are "exit nodes" to access the internet, but that's not it's primary function. Last time I tried it, it's slow as fuck.

There is the very real possibility that all of these anonymizing tools are in part or whole captured by government agencies. So, keep that in mind. I do not advocate the use of these tools for illegal activities, only to protect yourself when exercising your freedom of speech.
